name: Mark Shull

positions.statement: In answers to an OPB questionnaire for the May 2026 primary, Shull says he would keep county government lean, reduce regulation that raises housing and business costs, and prioritize core services without raising taxes.
positions.excerpt: keep county government lean, reduce the regulatory burden that drives up housing and business costs, and prioritize core services without raising taxes.

positions.statement: In answers to an OPB questionnaire for the May 2026 primary, Shull says he would work to attract jobs and businesses by keeping the regulatory environment business-friendly.
positions.excerpt: I'll work to attract jobs and businesses by keeping our regulatory environment business-friendly.

positions.statement: In answers to an OPB questionnaire for the May 2026 primary, Shull says unsheltered homelessness will not end with housing alone and calls for supportive housing, service coordination and prevention.
positions.excerpt: Unsheltered homelessness won't end with housing alone.

positions.statement: In answers to an OPB questionnaire for the May 2026 primary, Shull says homelessness efforts need better coordination with mental health and addiction services.
positions.excerpt: better coordination with mental health and addiction services

positions.statement: In answers to an OPB questionnaire for the May 2026 primary, Shull says he supports repealing Oregon's sanctuary state law.
positions.excerpt: I support repealing Oregon’s sanctuary state law

positions.statement: In answers to an OPB questionnaire for the May 2026 primary, Shull says he would oppose new county resolutions or ordinances that expand or symbolically strengthen sanctuary policies beyond state requirements.
positions.excerpt: Oppose any new county resolutions or ordinances that expand or symbolically strengthen sanctuary policies beyond state requirements.

positions.statement: In answers to an OPB questionnaire for the May 2026 primary, Shull says he does not support converting rural or resource lands into urban-style development.
positions.excerpt: I do not support converting rural or resource lands into urban-style development

positions.statement: In his voters' pamphlet statement, Shull describes himself as a decorated combat veteran and an advocate for veterans, among others.
positions.excerpt: I am a decorated combat veteran and a former small-business owner who successfully met payroll and created local jobs.

positions.statement: In his voters' pamphlet statement, Shull describes himself as a former small-business owner and an advocate for local businesses.
positions.excerpt: I am a relentless advocate for taxpayers, veterans, working families, and local businesses.

positions.statement: In a county-hosted candidate sheet from his 2024 Position 4 campaign, Shull says he would advocate for a healthy environment through timber management and wildfire mitigation.
positions.excerpt: Advocate for a healthy environment thru good timber management/wildfire mitigation

collection_notes: Items i1-i7 come from the OPB May 2026 primary questionnaire (text extracted from the PDF WebFetch saved; WebFetch's summary could not read it). Combined multi-issue searches were used for environment/energy/water/wildfire and small business/labor to save budget. A search summary suggested a data-centers moratorium, but in the pamphlet that text is in Paul Savas's column, not Shull's, so it was NOT used. Candidate-sheet item (i10) is from the 2024 Position 4 campaign (file metadata 2024); it names MarkSHULLUSA.com but that domain is not confirmed in the 2026 pamphlet, so website_url stays null. Identity: same Mark Shull (former Position 4 commissioner, retired Lt Col) as in the 2026 pamphlet.
